outline_section.section_title: Introduction to Convolution of Unequal-Width Rectangular Pulses
outline_section.learning_goal: Introduce why unequal-width rectangular pulses produce a trapezoidal convolution output and preview the workflow of breakpoints, overlap length, and amplitude scaling.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Make explicit that unequal widths create three nonzero overlap behaviors: growing overlap, full overlap at the shorter width, and shrinking overlap.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use two positive rectangular pulses with unit heights and unequal widths, with the shorter pulse sliding across the longer pulse.
paragraph_plan: State the convolution-as-overlap-area viewpoint for rectangular pulses.
Define the edge-aligned breakpoints that split t into no-overlap, growing-overlap, full-overlap, shrinking-overlap, and no-overlap regions.
Explain that the shorter width determines the plateau overlap length.
Explain that pulse amplitudes scale the overlap area after the overlap length is found.
Preview the final trapezoidal output as a piecewise function built from the three nonzero overlap regions.
display_math_plan: Show y(t)=A_xA_hL(t), where L(t) is the overlap length of the two rectangular supports.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep this section conceptual and compact; do not compute a full piecewise convolution before the example sections.

example_outline.variation_from_previous: Moves from conceptual overlap regions to the first executable task: locating the t-values that control every later piece.
solution_step_plan: Write the fixed support of x(tau) as 0\le \tau\le 4.
Write the shifted support of h(t-\tau) as t-7\le \tau\le t.
Set the right edge of h(t-\tau) equal to the left edge of x(tau) for first contact.
Set the right edge of h(t-\tau) equal to the right edge of x(tau) for the start of full overlap.
Set the left edge of h(t-\tau) equal to the left edge of x(tau) for the end of full overlap.
Set the left edge of h(t-\tau) equal to the right edge of x(tau) for last contact.
